title: Rafi and the Rolling Pumpkins
markdown:
Bright sunshine streamed through Rafi’s window! Birds chirped. Rafi bounced out of bed, grabbed his propeller cap, and dashed outside. Plum, his rabbit friend, twitched her nose.

"Plum!" Rafi called. "Look!"

A cart piled high with big, bright pumpkins sat stuck in the garden path. It wouldn’t budge.

“Oh my!” Plum nudged a pumpkin. It wobbled, but the cart stayed put.

Rafi gripped the cart. "Push, Plum! Push together!" They pushed and pulled, puffing hard. The cart clunked but wouldn't budge. "Oh, no!" Rafi sighed. "The pumpkins are too heavy!"

Mr. Reed, the wise badger, ambled over. "A sticky situation?" he chuckled.

“Mr. Reed!” Rafi exclaimed. “We can’t move this cart! The pumpkins are too heavy!”

Mr. Reed peered at the cart. "You're pushing the whole cart. Look at what’s helping it sit up."

Rafi and Plum tilted their heads. Round, black things were underneath.

“Wheels!” Plum squeaked.

“Exactly!” Mr. Reed beamed. “Wheels roll around and around! They help heavy pumpkins glide easily. Much easier than sliding!"

Rafi watched a wheel spin. *Spin, spin, spin!* It made the heavy cart move so easily! "The wheels!" Rafi exclaimed. He understood!

He gave the cart a gentle push by a wheel. WHOOSH! The cart glided, picking up speed! The smooth whirring of the wheels filled the air. Plum giggled and hopped alongside. "It's so easy now!" she chirped.

"Wow!" Rafi's eyes sparkled. "Wheels help us move big, heavy things! That's why they're such a clever invention!" They rolled the cart to the pumpkin patch, not even puffing.

"I wonder," Rafi mused, "what other amazing things are invented to help us?"

And with a grin, Rafi and Plum bounced off, eager to see what brilliant inventions they would discover today!
characters: Rafi the question asker, Plum the rabbit, Mr. Reed
